text:
The statement least likely to follow from Savigny’s Volksgeist is that a people’s spirit is too uniform and abstract to shape particular legal rules, so law is tied to culture only loosely and incidentally. Law developing gradually from a people’s customs and shared consciousness, and a society’s law reflecting its culture, both follow directly from that notion. Savigny treated the Volksgeist as the organic source of a nation’s concrete legal life, in the same way its language grows.
